findings.reason: Untrusted source: userspace write() to debugfs file /sys/kernel/debug/bna/pci_dev:*/regrd (registered via bnad_debugfs_op_regrd at line 449-455, file table entry line 483, S_IFREG|0644) fully controls nbytes and buffer contents. Violated invariant: line 315 memdup_user(buf, nbytes) allocates exactly nbytes bytes and copies nbytes bytes with no NUL terminator; nothing checks for an in-bounds NUL. Unsafe use: line 319 sscanf(kern_buf, "%x:%x", &addr, &len) is a C-string parser that scans past the allocation end when the user supplies nbytes non-NUL bytes, giving a slab out-of-bounds read (KASAN, info leak/crash), identical mechanism to the scsi bfa seed (same Brocade code lineage). Fix primitive present in-tree is memdup_user_nul, unused here. Counterevidence checked: no len+1 allocation, no strndup_user, no memchr/strnlen termination check anywhere in the function (lines 300-359 verified); regwr sibling below has the same defect. Permission is 0644 so any local user with debugfs read access can write if mounted rw; impact is OOB read only, register values returned via the regrd read path.

Same mechanism in bnad_debugfs_write_regwr: line 375 memdup_user(buf, nbytes) exact-size copy with no terminator, then line 379 sscanf(kern_buf, "%x:%x", &addr, &val) scans for NUL past the nbytes-sized heap buffer. Registered as debugfs 'regwr' with mode S_IFREG|0200 (line 484). Unfixed in s02; fix is memdup_user_nul. Counterevidence checked: full function lines 361-400 read, no termination guarantee anywhere.

candidates.reason: strcmp("cancel", vol_args->name) on memdup_user'd BTRFS_IOC_RM_DEV_V2 args, but btrfs_check_ioctl_vol_args_path/2_subvol_name (lines 230-242) enforce memchr(name, 0, sizeof(name)) != NULL before every strcmp/strchr/memparse use (checked at lines 1162, 1365, 1392, 2414, 2500, 2714, 2755, 2818); fixed-size struct member, not attacker-sized alloc.
strscpy from nla_data guarded by IPVS_DAEMON_ATTR_MCAST_IFN NLA_NUL_STRING policy (line 3199); destination is fixed sizeof(c.mcast_ifn).
strcpy(value->vstr, nla_data(param_data)) preceded by len = strnlen(nla_data, nla_len(param_data)) with rejection when len == nla_len (line 474-477), so NUL is guaranteed in-bounds.
strcpy(timeout->name, ...) with CTA_TIMEOUT_NAME policy NLA_NUL_STRING, .len = CTNL_TIMEOUT_NAME_MAX - 1 = 31, into name[32]; netlink core guarantees trailing NUL for NLA_NUL_STRING.

strcmp(name, nla_data(link[TIPC_NLA_LINK_NAME])) with left side checked by string_is_terminated(name, len) (line 584) and right side governed by tipc_nl_link_policy NLA_NUL_STRING (net/tipc/netlink.c:91).
strncmp on nla_data devname; ETHTOOL_A_HEADER_DEV_NAME policy is NLA_NUL_STRING with len ALTIFNAMSIZ-1 (lines 19-20, 27-28); bitset.c:402 same via bit_policy NLA_NUL_STRING (line 316).

sscanf(buf, "%d %5s", ...) in do_rbd_remove, but buf comes from sysfs/kernfs store (NUL-terminated page buffer), opt_buf[6] is pre-set to '\0' and %5s writes at most 5 chars + NUL; no usercopy in this path.
copy_from_user(str, buf, s) with s = min_t(u64, 64, size) into char str[65] that was memset to 0 first; at least one NUL byte always in-bounds.

ucma_set_option memdup_user(cmd.optval, cmd.optlen) with KMALLOC_MAX_SIZE check; optval consumed only by ucma_set_option_id/_ib with exact optlen-size checks and typed reads; no string helper touches optval.
sed_ioctl memdup_user(arg, _IOC_SIZE(cmd)) passed to structured struct-based parsers (opal_save, opal_set_new_pw, ...); no sscanf/strcmp/strnlen on the copied buffer.
memdup_user(param.addrs, param.addr_num) used only as sockaddr array in __sctp_setsockopt_connectx; binary parsing, no C-string consumption.
ffs_prepare_buffer memdup_user(buf, len); all string consumers (e.g. __ffs_data_do_strings line 3102) use strnlen(data, len) with explicit bounds and reject length == len.
vmemdup_user of vhost_vdpa_config config.len bytes written to device config space; binary byte-wise, no string helper.

limitations: The reported bnad_debugfs.c findings are debugfs .write file_operations handlers, the exact seed pattern in the bna sibling driver of scsi bfa; they surfaced from the tree-wide memdup_user-then-string-parser scan the intent permits, not from the ioctl/sockopt subset, whose targeted audit (btrfs ioctls, ucma set_option, sed-opal ioctl, sctp connectx, ethtool tunables, bluetooth/atm/ax25/can setsockopt, ipset/iptables netlink, devlink/tipc/ipvs/nfnetlink netlink attrs) found no site lacking a termination guarantee.

copy_from_user sites are numerous (~1112 files tree-wide; 198 in drivers/gpu/drm alone); only those co-located with C-string helpers in ioctl/sockopt/netlink/char-dev contexts were reviewed, so an unterminated-copy variant in an unexamined driver cannot be excluded.
compat_ioctl handlers, io_uring register paths, and most media/DVB ioctls were only pattern-scanned, not function-by-function read.
No compilation or dynamic testing was performed (snapshot is read-only); classification rests on source reading of the complete functions cited.
